parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is dominated by a national universal-exposure document regime: passports and visas are processed by birth-sex markers, X markers are barred, officers are instructed to refuse applications on document discrepancies and to consider permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility, and travellers report confiscation and stranding — an exposure every crossing carries. Federal custody adds documented severe harm (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men in immigration custody; conversion-model prison policies). The visited state/province itself is comparatively mild: no adult facility or care ban, no criminalisation, repealed sodomy statute, marriage recognition, four municipal ordinances. Consequences of outing are exclusion, refusal, humiliation and custody abuse if detained — not execution or routine imprisonment. This sits at the top of the Elevated Risk band: heavy universal entry exposure atop a moderate host jurisdiction.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: birth-sex marker rules, X markers blocked, refusal instructions on discrepancies, potential lifetime fraud finding, reported passport confiscation and stranding abroad; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Passport policy enjoined-then-reinstated litigation unresolved; civil-liberties union suit pending; existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry adjudication is national; state rules do not apply at the border. A document discrepancy at entry can escalate to fraud ineligibility before the state is ever reached.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented severe federal custody harm: immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national prison policies cutting hair, removing hormones, conversion-model therapy; reporting halted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Rescinded prison LGBTQ protections partially offset by the 2020 employment ruling; remedies unclear; several orders enjoined in court.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any entry refusal, visa investigation or fraud allegation can route a visitor into federal immigration custody where documented abuse applies.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; extensive state/province facility bans elsewhere; in this division, one school-district bathroom policy and a student sports ban, but no statewide adult facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statewide statute permits adult facility use per gender identity; 29+ state/provinces mapped without bans; the state bathroom trespass statute is in other divisions, not here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exposure depends on level: national facilities restricted; this division's adult facilities unrestricted by statute, though laws 'defining sex' may still affect access.

care_services.exposure: Youth-care restriction approved by governor-appointed medical board (draft, pending vetting and comment); national proposed rules barring public insurance for trans patients under 18; hospitals nationally subpoenaed for minors' records.
care_services.protection: No statewide ban on adult gender-affirming care; the youth measure is a recommendation plus draft, not operative.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor needing care faces pending state restriction plus national insurance rules; adult visitors face no documented state care ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National rhetoric frames gender-affirming care as 'mutilation', teachers' facilitation of transition as prosecutable, and 'radically pro-transgender' groups as counterterrorism priorities; 'gender ideology' materials purged; first known bathroom-law arrest elsewhere (handcuffed, men's ward).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Courts have blocked several orders; the stated counterterrorism powers exclude people who merely disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level threat framing is moderate (appointed boards); the heavier threat framing is national and shapes enforcement posture visitors encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling with a trans minor: national investigation/prosecution directives for facilitators, records subpoenas, 27 state/provinces with youth-care bans, student sports and school-district bathroom exclusions here.
minors_guardians.protection: This division's youth-care ban is not operative; no statewide youth-care statute; municipal conversion-therapy ban in one city.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian seeking care or school placement enters national scrutiny regimes; the state's draft rule could activate without legislative session.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No count of trans-specific violence in this division and no homicide denominator; state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; outside four municipalities no recourse against discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national employment discrimination prohibition; four municipal ordinances cover ~46% of population (enforcement undocumented).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor's recourse depends on locality: municipal ordinance coverage versus none statewide; state penalty enhancement unavailable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: final youth-care regulation text, reach of board sports rule beyond mapped categories, enforcement of municipal ordinances, state law-enforcement bias-crime guidance — all unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ on document rules exists; equality protections remain in 22 state/provinces plus capital district.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are partial and locality-dependent; unresolved litigation means operative rules can shift before or during travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier. Both feature routine universal identity exposure through document-linked systems and administrative friction, with punitive escalation possible (here, the fraud lifetime bar; there, a presentation statute) but custodial sentences uncommon. This jurisdiction's entry regime is harsher, offset by the host division's absence of any adult facility or care restriction.

Less severe. Karthovia's routine stops, passport and phone confiscation and compelled interviews target visitors on the street continuously; here the universal exposure concentrates at entry adjudication and custody, with no documented routine street policing of trans visitors and a mild host jurisdiction.

More severe. Kestrel Isles yields extended screening, humiliation and possible refusal — administrative outcomes with slow appeals. This regime adds lifetime fraud ineligibility, documented confiscation stranding travellers abroad, and documented abusive federal custody with sexual violence, placing it below 0.55.

Well below. Meridia's regime ends in brief detention and release with working tribunals and compensation. Here remedies at entry are unresolved litigation, a fraud ground carries permanent consequence, and custody abuse is documented — the mismatch between documented harm and functioning recourse is materially greater.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime pairs a nationally imposed, universal-exposure entry/document system — birth-sex markers, refusal instructions, fraud-finding leverage, reported stranding — with a host division that is among the milder ones: no adult facility or care ban, no criminalisation, marriage recognition, and partial municipal protections. The state layer neither compounds nor neutralises the national layer. The gravest documented harms (custody abuse, conversion-model prison policies) arise only once a visitor enters federal custody, via an entry refusal or investigation chain that the document regime makes plausible; frequency there is lower, severity extreme. Youth-specific national scrutiny adds family-travel exposure, though the division's own youth-care rule is not yet operative. Net: an Elevated Risk jurisdiction, above the 0.35 tier because consequences are exclusion and custody risk rather than routine detention or imprisonment, below the 0.55 tier because the universal exposure is real, escalating, and thinly remedied.
